items.q: Some people had asked me if I had ever seen or heard him. I hadn't so I asked for some information about him... So one Opportunity night I saw a fellow... I knew this must have been Brother Brodie and it was.

ctx.x: One amateur who became famous especially in New York at Connie's Inn was a young fellow named Earl Tucker. He had come from Baltimore and wore sailor pants and shoes with tap dancers taps on them. He was a double-jointed fellow and could twist his body like a snake dancer and tap dance at the same time. He could stand back on his leg in a way that one would think they were going to break and he won the first prize the first time he came to Opportunity night. People started calling him "Snake Hips" and it was not…

The most fantastic personality to take part in these amateur contests was a violinist called Brother Brodie. Some people had asked me if I had ever seen or heard him. I hadn't so I asked for some information about him and all that they would tell me was wait.......

So one Opportunity night I saw a fellow with a long back frock coat like the Jack-Legged Preachers wore and a violin case. He was a queer looking bird of a certain age and I knew this must have been Brother Brodie and it was.
